newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen opening mixed, no clear direction.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen opening mixed, no clear direction.

text.p: U.S. stocks should open mixed, with no clear indicators to set the market's tone after last week's expedition to new all-time highs. Friday's expiration of options could also spell a slightly lower opening.

"Well, we ended on the upside (Friday) and usually the following Monday after a closeout, you get the opposite kind of opening," said Hildegard Zagorski, Prudential Securities analyst. "So at the opening we could come down a little bit."
The long bond was up 5/32 to yield 6.45 percent and Standard & Poor's December futures fell 0.05 to 740.80.

On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose to another new all-time high, the eighth straight record close for the index, which settled up 35 to about 6348, pushed higher by screaming gains in IBM.

IBM rallied 8-1/8 to 145, its best finish since before the 1987 stock market crash. Nervousness has begun to build on Wall Street as more and more analysts wonder how long the fury of the roaring market can continue.
"I'm negative this week. We are headed, sometime this week, for a pullback of 200 to 250 points," said Peter Cardillo, director of research for Westfalia Investments.
"A pullback, taking us to 6100 or 6150, would be very healthy," he said.
No major economic data are due today.
Overseas, Tokyo stocks closed lower, off 133 points to 20,796 on the slowest volume so far this year. In London, the FTSE inched higher, up 3.8 to 3962.
U.S. stocks in London were steady, taking cues from the firm Treasury market.
The dollar was steady against the market but off session highs against the yen, with trading subdued by lack of fresh factors.
Among special situations, Mattel Inc said it agreed to buy Tyco Toys in a $755 million deal that would pay $12.50 for each Tyco share. Tyco shares closed at seven on Friday.
Tosco Corp agreed to buy Unocal's 76 products business for $1.4 billion and assume environmental liabilities. Tosco shares closed at 60-1/8 and Unocal shares closed at 39-1/2.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column says shareholders who invested alongside Ronald Perelman in Marvel Entertainment have seen their bonds and shares hacked to bits while the the financier profits.
The Treasury sells $28 billion in three- and six-month bills later this afternoon.
United Automobile Workers are expected to announce ratification results of General Motors contract vote.
The District Court holds a hearing on Norfolk Southern Corp suit to block the Conrail /CSX Corp merger.
